title: Why You Should Pay Yourself First
description: Before the month spends your money for you, give your future self a place in the plan.

sections.relatable_financial_problem: You receive your income and for a moment you feel relieved. Then the rent is due, electricity needs paying, transport must be covered, food has to be bought, and someone may need your help. You handle one expense after another and tell yourself that you will save whatever remains. But the month keeps moving. Small purchases add up, another bill appears, and suddenly payday is close again. You worked for the money, yet you cannot clearly see where it went. This experience is common, and it does not automatically mean you are careless. Often, the money simply had no clear plan before the spending began.
sections.escalating_real_world_stakes: When saving always comes last, it depends on chance. There may be nothing left after the essentials, or an unexpected expense may use the little amount you hoped to keep. Without a buffer, a broken phone, a medical expense, or a delayed payment can become a stressful emergency. You might have to borrow, postpone another bill, or ask someone for help. Then the next payday arrives already carrying yesterday's pressure. This cycle can make the future feel distant because every shilling seems to have an immediate demand. The problem is not that every person can save a large amount. The problem is relying on leftovers without first deciding what is realistic.
sections.clear_explanation_of_why_it_matters: Paying yourself first means deciding on an affordable amount for a goal before spending on things that are not essential. It is a simple order-of-priority change. Instead of waiting to discover whether money remains, you deliberately reserve a portion when income arrives. This does not mean ignoring rent, food, transport, debt payments, school fees, or other responsibilities. Those real needs must be considered first when you decide what is affordable. Paying yourself first is not a magic trick and it does not create extra income. It gives saving a defined place in your plan, so the decision is made intentionally rather than left to whatever happens at the end of the month.
sections.hopeful_and_realistic_possibility: Imagine that after reviewing your necessary expenses, you choose a modest amount that you can set aside regularly. You move it into a separate savings place and treat that transfer as one of the planned uses of your income. At first, the balance may look small. That is not a reason to dismiss the effort. A repeatable habit can help you prepare for irregular costs and make future choices with a little more breathing room. Some months may be difficult, and you may need to reduce or pause the amount when circumstances change. The goal is not to compete with anyone else's savings. The goal is to build a practical habit that fits your real life.
sections.practical_action_viewers_can_take: Here is a simple way to begin. Before your next payday, write down the expenses you must cover. Include food, housing, transport, utilities, debt commitments, and any important family responsibilities. Look honestly at what remains. Choose one small amount that will not put those essentials at risk. Decide exactly where you will keep it, preferably somewhere separate from the money you use every day. When income arrives, move that amount according to your plan, then organise the rest around your needs. If the amount is too difficult to maintain, make it smaller. If you cannot save this month, do not take on expensive debt just to follow a slogan. Review your budget and try again when it is practical.
sections.empowering_close: You do not have to start big, and you do not have to fix every part of your financial life today. Start deliberately. Give each shilling a purpose, protect the essentials, and make a realistic decision about the future. Over time, review the amount as your income, responsibilities, and priorities change. The real achievement is learning to make that decision before the money disappears. Your first deposit may be modest, but it represents a shift from hoping something will be left to planning for something that matters. Pay yourself first in a way that is safe, affordable, and sustainable. Your future deserves a place in today's plan.

hypothetical_examples.label: Hypothetical example
hypothetical_examples.text: Imagine someone who receives income and chooses a small, affordable amount to set aside before discretionary spending. The example illustrates a habit, not a promise about how quickly savings will grow.
